clue.text: Tragic ruin, almost destroyed by pick axe

parts.note: to pick is to choose or elect

indicators.note: destroyed says the letters of the following words are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order
almost says the word ruin loses its final letter before use

explanation.surface: A pickaxe has brought about a tragic ruin, nearly wrecking something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick axe' reads as one tool; split, 'pick' gives ELECT and 'axe' is the definition. 'almost' trims the ruin, and 'destroyed' signals the anagram; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Axe is musicians' slang for a guitar, especially the amplified kind used in rock.

clue.text: Some silly craze for skin-tight garments

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A passing fashion fad for clingy clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretchy synthetic fibre used for leggings and cycling shorts, standing here for the fabric of skin-tight clothes.

clue.text: Think about Tory blueprint

clue.text: Regular myth, rich in variety

indicators.note: in variety says the letters of the two words are mixed up into a different order

explanation.surface: An ordinary myth that is rich in different forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something regular has a steady repeating beat or pattern.

clue.text: Writer's dramatic end with fallen woman having no better alternative

parts.note: a fallen woman, in old moral language, is a harlot

explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' turns NO BETTER into TEBRONTE; the 's of Writer's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Jane Eyre, one of the three novelist sisters from Haworth in Yorkshire.

clue.text: See 1
Fault of girl's heartless longing

explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small fault or malfunction, especially in a machine or computer system.

clue.text: Police agent's chill-out time?

indicators.note: the 's stands for has: the words before it have the answer within them

explanation.definitionFit: A glacial period is literally a time when the world is chilled, punned on as relaxation time.

clue.text: Real gold with next credit report

explanation.surface: Genuine gold accompanied by the next credit statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for buying on credit; its sound gives TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something authentic is genuine, not fake or imitation.

clue.text: Spare pen is able to be slipped in

clue.text: A compiler from Ulster not quite drunk in Provence

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, is often called Ulster

parts.note: a crossword compiler is a setter

explanation.surface: A crossword setter from Northern Ireland is somewhat tipsy in southern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like the setter's state; it is the definition, as in a drink consumed in Provence.
explanation.definitionFit: An aniseed-flavoured liqueur, the kind of drink downed in the south of France.

clue.text: Born in a bad year after the end of the Raj, settled on Rochester

indicators.note: after says the following material comes behind that letter
the end of the word Raj is its final letter
in says one piece goes inside the other
bad says the letters of year are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: née, French for born, introduces a maiden name

explanation.surface: Someone born in a terrible year after the British Raj ended settled in Rochester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion; 'Raj' is British rule in India. In the novel, the heroine marries Mr Rochester.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brontë heroine who finally marries Edward Rochester, so she literally settles on him.

clue.text: The police operation needs right transport

indicators.note: operation says the letters of the words are worked on and reordered

clue.text: Local infestation by unknown people raised a threat to all

lice are a typical infestation

indicators.note: raised says the word is turned upwards, written backwards in a down clue

parts.note: men means people
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood bar overrun with vermin brought by strangers is a public menace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns MEN into NEM. 'Local' means a pub to British readers.
explanation.definitionFit: A notorious criminal or person regarded as a danger to the whole community.

clue.text: Appropriate alternative to flight in store?

explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to take something without permission, as a thief in a store does.

clue.text: Buddy has a club in Tinseltown

clue.text: What makes Tom feel a bit irritated?

definitions.text: What makes Tom feel a bit irritated?

explanation.walkthrough: Tom is a male cat; the whole clue both defines and builds the answer.

clue.text: One of two sound producers, each about right on Beethoven's third

indicators.note: on says the following piece is attached to that letter

parts.note: apiece means each

explanation.surface: A musical work, with each part about right, built on Beethoven's Third Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's third' looks like the Eroica symphony; it is just the letter E. 'about' puts R inside APIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: A headphone has a pair of these, each producing sound at one ear.

clue.text: Accommodate force

to force someone is to compel them to do something

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to do a favour for someone, and to compel someone to act.

clue.text: Somehow bear externally chirpy disposition under great pressure

indicators.note: externally says the rearranged chirpy goes around the outside
disposition, an arrangement, says the letters of chirpy are rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Describes conditions or chambers with gas at higher than normal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: O for a holiday as career!

clue.text: See 7
Instead of a threat

definitions.meaning: added as a warning, do it, otherwise there will be consequences
